problem: Vision-language semantic navigation has been studied mainly in household/office scenes; its feasibility and failure modes in unstructured construction sites with weak semantic regularities are unexplored, while construction robots still rely on geometry- or BIM-map-based navigation.
motivation: Construction tasks (e.g., object inspection) are specified at a high semantic level and prior maps are unreliable, so semantic zero-shot ObjectNav is appealing. It is unclear how perception quality versus VLM semantic guidance limit navigation performance in such sites.
key_idea: Deploy a VLFM-style zero-shot ObjectNav pipeline in a custom simulated construction site and run controlled substitutions of the perception model and exploration strategy to diagnose failure modes.
insight: Stronger perception (SAM3) raises SR from 33% to 58% and cuts FN/FP, but SPL stays low (38%) and NE rises (16% to 25%), so exploration efficiency is bottlenecked by weak, noisy VLM semantic cues in construction scenes. In the randomized Scene B the gap between SAM3 and baselines narrows and SPL collapses (e.g., 26% to 5% for P2), showing the bottleneck shifts from perception to semantic reasoning and exploration.
method: Frontier map: 2D top-down grid from depth and odometry marking occupied/free/explored cells; frontier midpoints serve as candidate waypoints.
Semantic value map: BLIP-2 cosine similarity between the RGB image and a target prompt is back-projected onto the FOV cells, fused across time with confidence-weighted averaging (VLFM).
Frontier selection: pick the frontier with highest semantic value in exploration mode; a greedy nearest-frontier variant serves as the non-semantic baseline.
Object detection and segmentation: YOLOv7 (COCO classes, threshold 0.8) or Grounding-DINO (non-COCO, threshold 0.4) plus Mobile-SAM; replaced by a unified SAM3 in the stronger variant.
Goal navigation: on detection, compute the nearest 3D point on the segmented object using depth and pose and approach it as a waypoint.
Local planner: DD-PPO/VER-trained PointNav policy takes distance and heading to the waypoint and outputs discrete actions.
Custom environment: Unity-built indoor construction site (~367 m², 26 categories) imported into Habitat, plus an LLM-layout-generated Scene B with re-randomized object placement.

setting.backbone: BLIP-2 (frozen) + YOLOv7/Grounding-DINO + Mobile-SAM (frozen) or SAM3 (frozen) + pretrained PointNav RL policy
setting.training_data: none (training-free; all models pretrained and frozen)
setting.action_space: discrete: Move Forward 0.25 m, Turn Left 30°, Turn Right 30°, Stop (500-step limit)
setting.simulator: Habitat with custom Unity-built construction scene

numbers.extra: custom simulated construction site, 12 target categories, 1 episode each

numbers_note: Custom benchmark with roughly 12 episodes per scene; no standard benchmark numbers. Note the NE column denotes 'Not Encountered' rate, not navigation error.
results: Semantic VLM guidance improves SR from 25% (frontier-only) to 33% in Scene A, and SAM3 perception raises it to 58% with SPL 38%. In Scene B, SR is 17/33/42% for P1/P2/P3 with very low SPL, showing that efficiency remains weak.
limitations: Small custom simulated benchmark (about 12 target objects per scene, single episode each) with no real-world validation.
VLM semantic guidance is unreliable under weak semantic relationships, causing frequent not-encountered failures and low SPL; no multi-floor support.
